chapters:
Fire Drill Friendship (2024–2025)
  - Inciting: Ines and Ishita meet at 2 a.m. at Meyer Green during a dorm fire alarm; they split a Coupa croissant coupon and compare calendars like passports. Alternating close thirds begin: Ines counts hours she owes Arrillaga; Ishita counts hours she owes Homeland Security.
  - Campus texture: EVGR and Stern contrasts; Huang Engineering Center whiteboards vs. Clark Center wet benches; Cantor’s Rodin Garden smoke-stung during September wildfires; N95 lines snaking by CAPS; Hoover Tower’s shadow as a day-length metronome.
  - Early tests: Mateo soft-launches a dorm analytics bot; Zadie tapes crisis flyers when CAPS cuts waitlists. Carlos teaches Ines knife skills and a union’s quiet power. Ishita trembles through first pipetting sessions in Farzaneh Lab; Slack pings at 1 a.m. become weather.
  - Election static and class splits: FAFSA-like “verification” emails flag Ines’s remittances; Ishita builds a CPT/OPT spreadsheet no one else wants to look at. Yifan’s unofficial office hours in Green Library whisper what official sites won’t.
  - First fracture line: Mateo poaches RA data; Zadie calls it a boundary. Ines refuses his “move fast” culture; Ishita stays late to fix mislabeled imaging files because refusal feels like a visa risk.

act_descr: Act turn: Atmospheric river floods basements; Ishita stays through alarms to move organoid dishes, earning Farzaneh’s attention. Ines ships an elegant ethics-check script for Naomi’s reporting; Naomi sees a bigger pattern. Friendship tightens in small, tired ways: meal-swipe trades, lakebed walks at dry Lagunita, a shared umbrella to Vaden. The cost meter starts ticking.
chapters:
Throughput (2026–2027)
  - New normal: AI/biotech collab between Farzaneh and Arjun’s stealth company “harmonizes” organoid signals. Ishita is asked to “preprocess” data so the Nature figure pops; Omar points out missing controls. Asha’s “how to say no” scripts land like vitamins no one wants to take.
  - Midpoint mirror: Ines’s audit tool helps Naomi connect grants to cap tables; a conflict thread leads back to Farzaneh’s startup equity. Carlos leads a dining walkout; burritos appear at Meyer Green like a parallel syllabus on care. Dean Klein unfurls dashboards and belonging scores while cutting counseling hours.
  - Pressures multiply: H‑1B odds turn lottery-myth; Yifan warns about CPT exploitation. Arjun invites Ishita to a “CPT‑compatible” role—Signal only, “impact first.” Ines, flagging after an aid “review,” couch‑surfs at Domingos’s shop office; showers before Arrillaga shifts, hair tie over the wrist scar. Mateo hires her under‑the‑table; she realizes he’s reselling mental‑health app telemetry for A/B ad tests and walks, broke but colder-eyed.
  - Naomi publishes: Inquiry hits the lab; Slack metadata surfaces late-night edits. Dean Klein pivots to reputation containment; Farzaneh frames it as “miscommunication.” Zadie unravels after a resident crisis, finally asking for help she’s been offering others; nosebleeds return for Ishita in the dry winds.

act_descr: Act crisis: A storm trashes Clark Center freezers; Ishita’s salvage makes her indispensable and visible to the wrong people. Arjun dangles day‑1 CPT myths; Priyanka and Sanjay forward success stories; Teresa leaves voice notes about Lisbon rents and saints. Ines misses one more verification email and loses a month of aid; Domingos says, “a job that needs your visa owns you.” Both hear it, differently.
chapters:
The Cost of Staying (2027–2028)
  - Lines drawn: The paper is accepted with Ishita mid‑author; a supplementary methods “tweak” needs her sign-off. Asha rehearses her refusal: precise, documented. Farzaneh threatens letters. Arjun offers a shadow H‑1B pipeline; Yifan says it will nuke consular renewals.
  - Theft made pretty: The university’s integrity dashboard launches—Ines’s prototype, repackaged and credited to a dean’s task force. Naomi leaks emails; legalese blooms. Ines must choose public fight (risk aid, jobs) or SoMa safety (Dogpatch bioincubators, badge access, silence). Ishita must choose to report doctored preprocessing (risk OPT, blacklist) or keep the pipeline intact.
  - Friendship fracture: A fight at Coupa—quiet, surgical. Ines calls it fraud wrapped in mentorship; Ishita calls it survival inside rules designed to fail her. They leave in opposite directions as Hoover Tower’s shadow stretches like a deadline.
  - Climax: Omar files a formal complaint with Slack time stamps; Ishita attaches her careful refusal. Inquiry expands; Farzaneh’s “impact first” becomes evidence. Arjun ghosts; Signal bubbles go gray. Ines goes public with Naomi, on-record and unadorned; Dean Klein offers a backroom credit and a future committee. Ines declines.
  - Fallout and small mercies: Layoffs ripple; safe internships weren’t. Zadie sleeps for real and returns with boundaries. Mateo pivots, again, alone. Carlos keeps the knives sharp. Teresa sends sardines and relief; Priyanka and Sanjay, shaken, stop forwarding odds and start asking costs.
  - Resolution: Commencement under smoke; masks over gowns. The Hoover shadow marks noon like a sundial on a hard year. Ishita stays on STEM OPT at a cautious employer Yifan vetted, visa clock loud but hers. Ines leaves the Valley for a job that doesn’t require a badge to belong, audit code in her pocket and her name on it. They don’t agree; they witness. A last scene at Terman Fountain: no promises, just calendars compared like truce flags and the shared knowledge of what it took to still be there.
